release: Davonium Technologies V44 — immersive Three.js website and five distinct core demos
source_folder: release source rebuilt from the user-provided V41 website package and corrected V43 baseline

checks.visual_browser_test: Headless Chromium screenshot attempt stalled in the environment; not claimed as passed.
checks.live_github_push: Not performed; deployment script requires user-authorized GitHub access.

results.threejs_robot: Procedural, hard-surface faceted helmet and articulated Three.js r186 character with gaze, blink, gesture, and speech-activity mouth/chest animation. Not an externally rigged GLB asset; speech timing is not phoneme accurate.
results.page_3d: Lazy page-specific Three.js hero scenes are defined for the five core demos and supporting company pages; homepage uses the robot scene and 3D orbital elements to avoid a second scene competing for WebGL resources.
results.themes: Content remains unchanged while theme-aware CSS changes backgrounds, surfaces, accent colours and 3D lighting.
results.intro: A skippable letter-by-letter glowing wordmark, typed-on main headline, and quiet synthesized chime. AudioContext waits for a real user gesture; no audio can be guaranteed before interaction due browser policies.
results.performance: Three.js loads when the hero scene is near the viewport. Rendering pauses when hidden or out of view, lowers pixel ratio on small/low-power devices, respects reduced motion and provides static fallback artwork. CDN connectivity is required for WebGL scenes.
results.security: directory.md remains in the local ZIP and is omitted from the public working tree/commit by deployment exclusions. Common credential files are excluded; this is a filename/path audit, not a guarantee that no secret-like string can appear in source.
results.deployment: External launcher extracts release and starts the matching PowerShell publisher. Publisher targets DavoniumTech/davoniumtech-corporate-site main, backs up the source and old main, excludes directory.md and known credential patterns, stages/audits file paths, asks user to type PUSH, and uses non-force Git push then verifies remote main SHA. It does not set DNS or GitHub Pages settings.
tests_not_done: Visual headless Chromium capture was blocked/stalled in the provided environment; no verified automated screenshot was produced.
No real-device Android, iOS, tablet, desktop GPU or assistive-technology tests were performed.
Three.js is fetched lazily from jsDelivr; first-load 3D requires CDN network access. A static robot/art fallback is supplied.

Browser speech synthesis uses voices available on the visitor device; the code excludes Indian English/Hindi voices from automatic selection but available voices differ by OS. No speech begins without a visitor action.

The deployment script has not been executed against GitHub from this session; the user must authenticate and approve the explicit PUSH prompt. GitHub Pages/Cloudflare Pages settings and DNS are not changed by the script.
